candidates.sector_or_industry: OSAT / advanced semiconductor packaging and test
candidates.theme_relation: If CoWoS-like and high-end package capacity remains scarce, OSATs with credible advanced packaging ramps can become second-source or overflow capacity beneficiaries.
candidates.why_include: Amkor is a US-listed OSAT with explicit advanced-packaging expansion plans, including a US high-volume advanced packaging facility. The link to AI/HPC is strong, but exact exposure to HBM-attached flagship accelerators needs customer/program verification.

candidates.next_evidence: Check ASE filings and calls for advanced packaging revenue, AI/HPC customer mix, FOCoS/CoWoS-related volumes, capex by site, and margin uplift from advanced packaging versus traditional assembly/test.

candidates.theme_relation: ASE can benefit if AI accelerator demand expands beyond TSMC internal CoWoS capacity or if advanced packaging/test outsourcing grows with chiplet and HBM package complexity.
candidates.why_include: ASE is a major US-listed ADR in OSAT and has explicit AI/HPC advanced-packaging initiatives. Its relevance is high, but the exact share of AI accelerator/HBM package revenue and customer allocation needs deeper evidence.

candidates.next_evidence: Quantify advanced packaging revenue contribution, tool categories used in HBM/CoWoS-like flows, order growth from memory customers, and whether HBM-related spend is incremental or cannibalizing other WFE.

candidates.theme_relation: HBM and 2.5D/3D packaging ramps require process tools, materials engineering, TSV/micro-bump/interposer-related capabilities, and faster yield learning.
candidates.why_include: Applied is not an HBM producer, but it is positioned upstream of the HBM and advanced-packaging capacity ramp. Its direct SK hynix HBM collaboration makes the node link stronger than generic wafer-fab equipment exposure.

candidates.next_evidence: Track advanced packaging and IC substrate tool orders, customer concentration in memory/foundry/OSAT, management commentary on AI-driven packaging demand, and signs of tool lead-time constraints.

candidates.theme_relation: As HBM stacks and large 2.5D packages become more complex and expensive, yield learning and defect control become critical bottleneck mitigators.
candidates.why_include: KLA is a second-order chokepoint candidate: its tools do not create HBM supply directly, but process control is critical when advanced packaging yield, substrate quality, and heterogeneous integration complexity constrain finished accelerator output.

memory_update.text: Add MU as a direct US-listed HBM candidate for the AI accelerator/HBM/advanced-packaging node; highest evidence strength among new US-listed names due to specific NVIDIA and AMD platform announcements.
Add AMKR and ASX as OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity candidates; both need deeper verification of exposure to flagship HBM-attached AI accelerators versus broader advanced-packaging markets.
Add AMAT and KLAC as upstream equipment/process-control candidates tied to HBM, 2.5D/3D packaging, IC substrates, and yield learning rather than direct accelerator unit shipments.

For this node, distinguish direct chokepoint suppliers from second-order enablers: direct = HBM vendors and advanced-packaging/test capacity; second-order = tools, inspection/metrology, materials, substrates, and yield-learning systems.

Still need a follow-up pass on US-listed or US-accessible substrate/material names, thermal-interface materials, test-equipment vendors, EDA/IP, and smaller specialty tool suppliers; some may be below $1B or non-US-listed.

node: AI accelerators, HBM memory, and advanced packaging stack
summary: Expanded the universe around the HBM plus advanced-packaging chokepoint. The highest-relevance US-listed additions are not only accelerator designers, but HBM suppliers, OSAT/advanced-packaging capacity providers, and packaging/process-control equipment vendors. Micron is the most direct US-listed HBM exposure; Amkor and ASE add outsourced advanced-packaging/test capacity exposure; Applied Materials and KLA are second-order equipment/process-control suppliers tied to HBM, 2.5D/3D packaging, IC substrates, yield learning, and capacity ramps. These are research candidates only, not trading recommendations.
